paragraphs: The route challenge system in The Paddle Games tracked whether you'd completed a route. Didn't tell you how fast, how many times, or where you ranked. Badge earned, nothing else.

I added gate-to-gate timing from Strava's streams API, completion history, personal records, and a leaderboard per route. Then immediately shipped a bug where loop routes were logging two-second lap records. The finish gate overlaps the start on a loop, so the algorithm found it a few GPS points after finding the start. Fix: a minimum-distance guard derived from the route's geometry.
If you paddle (SUP, kayak, canoe, surf, row, anything), connect your Strava account and join at thepaddlegames.com.
Anyone else hit the overlapping-gates problem when building gate-based timing?

tweets: Added gate-to-gate route timing and per-route leaderboards to The Paddle Games. Start gate, finish gate, 85% route coverage required to count as a completion. Completion history, personal records, ranked leaderboard per route.

Then shipped a bug: loop routes were logging two-second lap records. Start and finish gates overlap on a loop, so the algorithm found the "finish" just after finding the start, before anyone had moved. Fix was a minimum-distance guard derived from the route geometry.

If you SUP, kayak, canoe, surf, or row, connect your Strava account at thepaddlegames.com. Architecture post -> dimeglio.dev/blog/2026-05-26-every-named-route-now-has-a-leaderboard | @the.paddle.games on Instagram
